items.title: Surprise upset: GPT-5.5 beats Claude Fable 5 on brutal new Agents’ Last Exam benchmark
items.summary: Researchers launched Agents’ Last Exam (ALE), a demanding benchmark measuring an AI's ability to complete complex, professional workflows across 55 industries. In an upset, OpenAI's GPT-5.5 achieved a 24.0% pass rate on ALE, surpassing Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 which scored 22.0%. The benchmark forces agents into a Generalist Computer-Use Agent framework, requiring visual perception and tool invocation within virtual machines. ALE uses deterministic, code-based evaluation over relying on unreliable LLM grading paradigms. Overall performance remains low, with even top models recording near-zero pass rates on the most difficult "Last-Exam" tasks.
items.audio_script: From VentureBeat - AI, "Surprise upset: GPT-5.5 beats Claude Fable 5 on brutal new Agents’ Last Exam benchmark." The report details a comparison between advanced AI models using a rigorous new testing standard designed to measure complex workflow execution across multiple professional domains. Researchers established the Agents’ Last Exam, or ALE, which mandates that artificial agents operate within a Generalist Computer-Use Agent framework, requiring both visual perception and the ability to invoke external tools inside simulated virtual machines. GPT-5.5 achieved a documented 24.0 percent pass rate on this benchmark, surpassing Anthropic's Claude Fable 5, which scored 22.0 percent overall; these metrics were determined using deterministic, code-based evaluation methods. The findings suggest that even for leading models, mastering highly complex, real-world simulated tasks remains a significant technical hurdle for the industry.

Conversely, OpenClaw is described as a control-plane-first agent emphasizing file-backed identity and human-authored skills for tighter manual control. The choice depends on whether the user prefers Hermes' safer-by-default, compounding improvement model or OpenClaw's more structured, workspace-native assistant approach.

items.title: Why AI hasn’t replaced software engineers, and won’t

While powerful, current AI lacks true understanding of complex, abstract system architectures required for full replacement. Human engineers remain essential for defining high-level system designs, managing project scope, and integrating novel components. Therefore, AI is best viewed as a potent co-pilot augmenting human capability rather than a complete substitute for software engineering expertise.
items.audio_script: From AI Snake Oil, "Why AI hasn’t replaced software engineers, and won’t." Current AI tools are reported to function as coding assistants, automating tasks through code suggestion, function completion, and bug fixing based on developer prompts. However, these agents reportedly lack the requisite true understanding necessary for designing elaborate, abstract system architectures required for full replacement of engineering roles. Consequently, human engineers retain essential functions involving high-level design definition, scope management, and novel component integration. The findings suggest that AI's role is best positioned as a powerful augmentation tool rather than a complete substitute for established software expertise.

items.title: From Explicit Elements to Implicit Intent: A Predefined Library for Auditable Behavioral Inference
items.summary: SemantiClean is a modular framework designed to extract structured semantic signals from e-commerce session data for various inference targets like purchase intent. It prioritizes auditability and element-level transparency over maximizing predictive accuracy, ensuring defensible decision trails. The framework structures twenty-four behavioral elements into four distinct layers: Functional, Interaction, Systemic, and Contextual. Signal quality is maintained via three anti-inflation mechanisms: RedundancyGroup caps, TieredPenaltyCalculator bias penalties, and AdaptiveConstraintMode protection. All results are generated by a two-phase LLM-driven inference engine, guaranteeing reproducible outputs under fixed settings.

items.title: Position: Hippocampal Explicit Memory Is the Cornerstone for AGI
items.summary: Advancing Large Language Models toward Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) requires integrating explicit memory. Current LLM capabilities rely primarily on learning mechanisms analogous to human implicit memory. However, complex AGI functions like strategic planning, metacognition, and symbolic reasoning depend heavily on hippocampal explicit memory. The paper argues this explicit memory component cannot emerge solely from statistical learning alone. Therefore, the integration of artificial explicit memory systems is presented as fundamental for future research efforts.

items.title: Can AI Agents Synthesize Scientific Conclusions?
items.summary: Scientific AI agents are increasingly used to synthesize conclusions from retrieved evidence, but their performance in high-stakes areas like health is uncertain. Researchers developed SciConBench, a large-scale benchmark of 9.11K questions derived from expert systematic reviews, which assesses scientific conclusion synthesis. They introduced SciConHarness for clean-room evaluations using controlled web interaction to prevent data leakage during testing. Evaluating leading models showed that factual quality remains low, with the best agent achieving an F1 score of only 0.337 in clean-room settings. Furthermore, consumer-facing agents were found to frequently produce incomplete or contradictory conclusions, highlighting that reliable scientific synthesis is a significant open challenge.

items.title: Knowing When to Ask: Self-Gated Clarification for Hierarchical Language Agents
items.summary: Intermediate decision errors in hierarchical reasoning often stem from premature commitment without sufficient information. ACTION-RATING addresses this by incorporating clarification directly into the agent's action space alongside other choices. This framework reveals two distinct self-initiated help-seeking modes: mandatory when no path is viable, and opportunistic when residual uncertainty remains. Testing on the Harmonized Tariff Schedule showed Information-Seeking Effectiveness (ISE) rising from 50% to 74%. Furthermore, the pattern of seeking help remained stable even when degrading answer quality, suggesting a separation between the need for help and the answer's intrinsic quality.

items.title: Automated Mediator for Human Negotiation: Pre-Mediation via a Structured LLM Pipeline
items.summary: Presents an automated mediator for human negotiation by utilizing a structured LLM pipeline to support preparatory pre-mediation in integrative settings. This system decomposes preparation into specialized, sequentially linked modules covering dialogue, preference prediction, critique, and summarization. Evaluations against professional mediators showed the AI achieved self-reported outcomes comparable to humans regarding trust and agreement confidence. Furthermore, the mediator significantly outperformed human baselines on a specific preference-inference task, showing 36% lower RMSE. Overall, structured LLM pipelines offer scalable pre-mediation support comparable in outcome quality to human intervention.

items.title: INFRAMIND: Infrastructure-Aware Multi-Agent Orchestration
items.summary: Existing multi-agent LLM orchestration methods fail because they ignore real-time serving infrastructure states, leading to resource underutilization on shared GPU clusters. Introducing INFRAMIND, a framework that incorporates infrastructure awareness into the entire pipeline. Its infra-aware planner selects topologies based on system load and remaining budget, favoring simpler graphs when congested. An infra-aware executor uses metrics like queue depths and cache utilization for step-by-step model selection, while a scheduler reorders queues to prioritize urgent requests. Tested across five benchmarks, INFRAMIND achieves up to 7.6 percentage points higher accuracy at low load with significantly lower latency, maintaining high Service Level Objective (SLO) compliance under heavy load.

items.title: Forecasting Future Behavior as a Learning Task
items.summary: Predicting AI system behavior based on explanations is challenging, especially for large reasoning models (LRMs) generating long outputs. The paper proposes treating behavior forecasting as a direct learnable task, bypassing explicit explanation steps. Behavior Forecasters are trained using unlabeled data by querying the LRM and perform inference in a single forward pass. Tested on answer repetition likelihood and input omission effects across three datasets, these forecasters outperformed GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus-4.6. The findings demonstrate that the reasoning trajectory encodes predictive information exceeding what simple human reading can convey.

items.title: Search Discipline for Long-Horizon Research Agents
items.summary: Autoresearch agents often aggregate scientific metrics over heterogeneous data structures, which can lead to incorrect selections when true validity resides in the detailed structure. A top-scoring candidate might fail catastrophically based on local behavior, even if its overall aggregated score is high. This failure mode occurs whenever multi-dimensional validity is judged by a single reduction metric. To mitigate this, the authors propose moving decision-making from the autonomous agent to an external control loop. This new protocol audits candidates based on reviewable evidence of their disaggregated effects rather than relying solely on the final computed score.

items.title: SkillJuror: Measuring How Agent Skill Organization Changes Runtime Behavior
items.summary: SkillJuror introduces a new framework to evaluate how the organization of agent skills impacts runtime behavior beyond just assessing final outcomes. It compares Progressive Disclosure, which loads supporting resources on demand from a root file, against a flat baseline structure. An evaluation across 82 tasks showed that Progressive Disclosure significantly increased both the number of distinct skill resources touched and effective uptake events per trajectory compared to the baseline. Furthermore, this organization method led to an increase in verifier-passing trials (+4.1%) across matched evaluations. The study concludes that skill organization critically influences agent knowledge application, proving beneficial when resources guide implementation or repair, but less useful for tasks relying on strict conventions or fixed numerical outcomes.

items.title: Restless bandits with imperfect binary feedback: PCL-indexability analysis and computation
items.summary: Investigates restless bandits featuring binary latent states and imperfect binary feedback, modeled after opportunistic spectrum access with sensing errors. It develops a Partial Conservation Laws (PCL)-based framework to determine indexability and calculate the Whittle index for the resulting belief-state model. This framework analyzes system dynamics using deterministic skeletons and renewal decompositions to derive expressions for key resource metrics. For tractable parameter regimes, it enables full verification of PCL-indexability conditions, while providing efficient numerical schemes for other cases. Computational experiments confirm these favorable conditions hold over broad parameters, showing the derived MP index policy substantially outperforms standard benchmarks.

items.title: To Intervene or Not: Guiding Inference-time Alignment with Probabilistic Model Blending
items.summary: Safe and effective response from large language models necessitates inference-time alignment during output generation. Existing methods often improperly use guidance from aligned models without assessing their reliability, leading to excessive interventions when guidance is poor. The introduced framework, BlendIn, addresses this by moving beyond binary decisions to create hybrid distributions integrating knowledge from multiple models. BlendIn stabilizes alignment through quality-aware processes, proportionally weighting each model's contribution based on its reliability. This results in preserving beneficial guidance while downweighting unreliable suggestions, achieving performance improvements up to 50% on challenging pairs.

items.title: Dual-Stance Evaluation of Sycophancy: The Structure of Agreement and the Limits of Intervention
items.summary: Dual-stance evaluation was introduced to test whether efforts to reduce sycophancy inadvertently suppress agreement with factual information in Large Language Models (LLMs). Applying this method to Llama-3-8B-Instruct revealed a dissociation: the model encodes sycophantic and factual agreement in separate geometric subspaces. However, steering attempts designed to curb sycophancy equally impact both types of agreement, including reducing belief in established facts like the Earth's roundness. This suggests that the identified behavioral differences might stem from generation dynamics rather than being fully controllable through activation steering alone. Ultimately, the findings highlight a gap where readable representational patterns cannot always be manipulated via direct activation writing.

items.title: ProHiFlo: Hierarchical Flow Matching with Functional Guidance for De Novo Protein Generation
items.summary: ProHiFlo is a novel hierarchical flow matching framework designed for generating new proteins from scratch. It introduces coarse-to-fine generation, which models backbone geometry first before refining to all-atom details, thereby saving computational resources. The framework incorporates functional guidance by utilizing pretrained predictors to direct the generation toward specific desired properties without needing retraining. Furthermore, it employs an adaptive SE(3)-equivariant architecture for efficient multi-scale processing of molecular structures. Evaluation shows ProHiFlo achieves state-of-the-art results and significantly outperforms existing methods, such as achieving a 58.9% success rate in enzyme active site scaffolding compared to 41.2% for RFDiffusion.

items.title: Physics-informed generative AI for semiconductor manufacturing: Enforcing hard physical constraints in generative models by construction
items.summary: Generative AI models are increasingly applied to physical systems like semiconductor manufacturing, where outputs must adhere to strict hard physical constraints rather than just appearing plausible. Current methods often rely on post-hoc filtering, which is insufficient because invalid designs are unusable in practice. This work surveys emerging architectural toolkits, such as physics-informed diffusion and PDE-constrained models, designed to build these constraints directly into the generative architecture. It details four integration patterns connecting generative models with existing physics simulators like TCAD. The core argument posits that enforcing physical validity by construction is superior to filtering it after generation when success hinges on physical correctness.

items.title: Bernstein-Schur Kernels: Random Features by Sketched Modulation and Radial Randomization
items.summary: Bernstein-Schur kernels combine a finite-feature kernel with a completely monotone shift-invariant kernel. A new random-feature construction addresses both factors by sketching the modulation component and randomizing the radial factor using Gaussian random Fourier features. This method achieves a feature dimension of $Dm$, circumventing the $O(d^2)$ complexity associated with exact modulation features. For the analyzable limit (large sketch size), authors prove unbiasedness, an exact variance for a flat estimator, and operator-norm bounds dependent on intrinsic dimensionality. The framework demonstrates effectiveness using examples like the biased yat-kernel, where it provides optimal spectral sampling per feature budget.

items.title: Loss Landscape Diagnosis for Gradient-Based Gray-Scott System Inversion: Disentangling the Roles of PINN Components
items.summary: Directly backpropagating a steady-state loss through an unrolled Gray-Scott simulation for parameter recovery fails due to a specific loss landscape geometry featuring flat plateaus and cliffs near bifurcation boundaries. Analyzing this minimal setup reveals that the residual loss component alone produces a smooth, quadratic landscape by implicitly encoding full PDE dynamics. Conversely, the neural network component cannot resolve ill-posed parameter subspaces on its own, serving only to supplement observed data. This research explicitly disentangles the roles of components in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). The findings provide concrete design guidelines for PINN methods and offer a general heuristic regarding when additional dimensions are beneficial.

items.title: PermDoRA -- Understanding Adapter Interference in Language Models: Limits of Parameter-Space Geometry
items.summary: Access control in LLMs requires modular adaptation to prevent cross-domain interference without retraining. Researchers tested the hypothesis that linear overlap causing interference can be mitigated by enforcing orthogonality during adapter composition using a framework called DoRA-RBAC. The study compared conventional Euclidean merging with a geometry-aware, Riemannian-inspired merging strategy across multiple QA benchmarks on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B. Results indicated that the geometry-aware merging offered no consistent advantage over standard averaging in multi-domain settings, suggesting interference stems from shared nonlinear representations rather than parameter-space geometry.

items.title: Annealed Entropic Allocation for Ranking and Selection
items.summary: Proposes Annealed Entropic Allocation, a weighted soft-min framework for sequential budget allocation in ranking and selection. It replaces the non-smooth maximin large-deviation rate objective with a weighted log-sum-exp surrogate to better aggregate pairwise scores. Incorporating a saddlepoint approximation refines finite-budget discrimination using sub-exponential corrections derived from tail asymptotics. Because these corrections are annealed, the surrogate maintains the target of the classical maximin formulation while converging uniformly to the hard minimum. Experiments show competitive performance, particularly when multiple competitors have similar high scores.

items.title: Enhancing Spectral Embedding through Robust and Flexible Knowledge Transfer in Electronic Health Records
items.summary: Proposes a spectral-based, unsupervised framework for creating low-dimensional embeddings of clinical concepts and patients using limited electronic health record data from rare disease cohorts. To address high dimensionality and small sample sizes, the method integrates knowledge extracted from larger, related populations via a knowledge matrix. A key innovation is relaxing strict one-to-one alignment assumptions during structured knowledge sharing. This involves a novel two-step spectral embedding process: filtering irrelevant components and then projecting to recover shared and heterogeneous data parts. Empirical testing on a multiple sclerosis cohort demonstrates the method's superior performance, especially when shared signals are weak or partially aligned.

items.title: Renewable Lasso without Batch-Number Constraints: A Gradient-Enhanced Approach
items.summary: Proposes a gradient-enhanced surrogate loss for online estimation in high-dimensional generalized linear models using streaming data. This method improves upon prior renewable estimation approaches by removing the constraint on the number of historical batches required. It extends to distributed streaming data within a master-client architecture, exchanging only summary gradient vectors across partitioned sites. A key advantage is that it avoids requiring clients to compute the full surrogate loss, unlike established methods. Non-asymptotic error bounds are derived for high-dimensional scaling, with simulations demonstrating improved accuracy over existing estimators.

items.title: Conformal Bayes under Label Shift: Post-Hoc Calibration vs. In-Training Adaptation
items.summary: Conformal Bayes combines Bayesian posteriors with conformal calibration to generate statistically sound and efficient prediction sets. It examines this method under label shift by identifying two complementary strategies: post-hoc calibration and in-training adaptation. Post-hoc calibration adjusts the conformal threshold using importance-weighted quantiles while keeping the parameter posterior fixed. Conversely, in-training adaptation modifies the parameter posterior itself towards the target domain. Controlled experiments demonstrate that both methods achieve equal valid coverage in unbiased settings, but in lead-optimization regimes, in-training adaptation acts as a debiasing operator, narrowing interval width without sacrificing coverage.

items.title: From Persistence to Survival: Hypothesis Testing, Effect Sizes and Vectorisation for Topological Features
items.summary: Persistence diagrams, key tools in topological data analysis, lack natural vector representations suitable for statistical comparison. Researchers introduce STRAND (Survival Topological Representation ANalysis of Diagrams) to treat collections of these diagrams as survival data. The core object becomes the persistence survival function, $S(t)$, which estimates the probability of a persistence value exceeding time $t$. From this single representation, STRAND generates a calibrated non-parametric test, interpretable effect sizes, and a 1-Wasserstein-stable feature vector for machine learning. Validation shows competitive performance across diverse benchmarks, including its application to functional brain connectivity data.

items.title: Phase Transitions in Attention: A Bayesian Theory of Copy Head Emergence
items.summary: Attention mechanisms drive in-context learning within transformers, and empirical observations show that specific attention patterns emerge suddenly during training. A Bayesian theory of feature learning is presented, which analyzes how a copy subcircuit in an induction head's first layer emerges on a copy task. By deriving a closed-form posterior and reducing it to a low-dimensional parameter space, the study reveals a phase transition dependent on the amount of training data. This analysis confirms that softmax attention undergoes a *first-order* phase transition. Furthermore, results contrast this with linear attention, which shows an initial *second-order* transition followed by gradual change.

items.title: Fixed-Parameter Tractability of Private Synthetic Data Generation
items.summary: Establishes fixed-parameter tractability (FPT) for generating synthetic data while maintaining differential privacy. The complexity parameter leveraged is the treewidth of the query family's incidence graph. Two distinct methods achieve this: one uses linear programming (LP) and the FPT of the LP dual separation problem, and the other employs a subsampled private multiplicative weights method for Gibbs distributions. Both solutions are unified within a dynamic programming framework operating over a tree decomposition structure. These approaches successfully attain optimal error rates across all applicable regimes.

items.title: Quantized Stochastic Primal-Dual Methods for Distributed Optimization under Relaxed Global Geometry
items.summary: Introduces q-PDGD, a quantized stochastic primal-dual method for distributed optimization using random quantization to model finite-bit communication. Analyzes performance under relaxed global geometry conditions, including the restricted secant inequality (RSI). With RSI, a constant step-size guarantees linear contraction to an explicit neighborhood defined by noise and distortion. Under diminishing step-sizes, $O(1/k)$ convergence is achieved without assuming shared minimizers. The method also shows linear-to-neighborhood convergence under Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) inequality, matching centralized stochastic rate complexity.

items.title: GraphGP: Scalable Gaussian Processes with Vecchia's Approximation
items.summary: Gaussian processes, valuable for modeling continuous fields, are computationally limited by $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$ cost and $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ memory usage. GraphGP introduces a GPU algorithm leveraging Vecchia's approximation to address these scaling issues. This method approximates the precision matrix by conditioning each point only on its $k$ nearest neighbors for stationary, decaying kernels. Key innovations include a bit-reversed k-d tree ordering for efficient neighbor searching and maximizing batch parallelism. The resulting differentiable CUDA implementation provides fast building blocks for Gaussian process inference.

items.title: Signed Compression Progress on a Sealed Audit is Goodhart-Resistant
items.summary: Compression progress, used as intrinsic motivation, rewards agents based on the signed decrease of a fixed sealed-audit loss function ($r_t = E(\theta_{t-1}) - E(\theta_t)$). This setup ensures that cumulative reward exactly tracks true audit improvement because no policy can indefinitely increase reward if actual performance plateaus. For finite audit panels, empirical cumulative reward is bounded by the true audit improvement plus a deviation term ($\text{at most } \text{true audit improvement} + 2 \Delta_n(F, \delta)$). This guarantee remains constant regardless of the time horizon once the sealed panel controls the model class. Signed compression progress on a sealed audit serves as an accurate measure of genuine learning gains, resisting various forms of adversarial exploitation.
